entries.content: joy (d-7) Or 'thou shalt have joy and rejoicing.'
Lord, (e-8) 'Jehovah.' from (f-28) The Greek preposition indicates the time from when it would take place. see Gal. 1.15.

Lord (e-35) 'Jehovah.' to (g-24) En. but 'through' would suppose other men, whereas it is here characteristic merely of their own new path. The word for 'thoughts' here is that for 'practical wisdom.'
tidings (i-29) Or 'to bring the glad tidings of these things.' Lit. 'evangelize these things.'

which (k-30) 'Which are such as shall be.' giving the character, not merely a relative pronoun. I have imitated an expression of the Authorized Version, by adding the article, which though somewhat antiquated, gives in a measure the idea of character, and may serve to distinguish the sense; so ch. 10.42.
temple. (b-23) Naos, the shrine. recognised (l-14) As 'know,' Matt. 7.16.
what (a-16) 'Of what nature or character.' what the aim or meaning of it was.
Highest; (b-12) 'Highest' is a name, Hebrew Elyon. I notice therefore the absence of 'the.' see Gen. 14.18. God (c-16) 'Jehovah Elohim.' only occurrence in the Gospels.
ages, (d-12) Or 'for ever;' but it is plural.
deliverance (b-7) Or 'salvation.' 'Saved' in ver. 74 is a different word. but the same as 'our deliverer from the coming wrath,' 1Thess. 1.10.
deliverance (b-1) Or 'salvation.' 'Saved' in ver. 74 is a different word. but the same as 'our deliverer from the coming wrath,' 1Thess. 1.10.
fulfil (c-2) 'To work,' or 'accomplish.' what the fathers had lived on by faith as promised mercy. 'Your father Abraham saw my day and was glad.'
deliverance (b-5) Or 'salvation.' 'Saved' in ver. 74 is a different word. but the same as 'our deliverer from the coming wrath,' 1Thess. 1.10.
Lord (a-7) Lord (a-17) 'Jehovah.' by (b-10) Lit. 'stood all at once by them.'
Lord (a-45) 'Jehovah.' shepherds (d-16) Lit. 'the men the shepherds '
in (g-4) En. see Matt. 3.11. temple; (h-9) Hieron, as Matt. 4.5.
Lord (i-1) Despotes. see Note a, Acts 4.24.
Lord, (c-12) Some authorities read 'God.' Lord, (d-12) 'Jehovah,' as chs. 1.38; 3.4
business? (e-27) Lit. 'To be in the things of my Father.' Elsewhere in New Testament the expression ('to be in the things') only occurs in 1Tim. 4.15.
words (g-10) Logos. something more than 'words;' see Note to 1Cor. 1.5. prophet. (h-14) Isa. 40.3. ye (a-23) Or 'Make ye ready,' as ch. 1.76.
with (c-33) En, 'in the power of.' see Matt. 3.11.
by (a-15) En, 'in the power of.' see ch. 3.16.
Lord. (d-8) 'Jehovah;' 'do homage' here is proskuneo. 'serve' is latreuo. see Matt. 4.10.
but (a-9) 'But' here has the sense of 'but it is only' or 'no one else than.' see Gal. 1.7 and 19.
but (a-21) 'But' here has the sense of 'but it is only' or 'no one else than.' see Gal. 1.7 and 19.
power (c-21) Exousia and dunamis. see Matt. 10.1.
Master, (b-7) 'One who is over others,' not 'teacher.' see ch. 9.33. Only used of Christ and only by Luke.
partners (c-6) Metochos, ver. 7; koinonos, ver. 10. see Notes, Heb. 2.14.
partners (c-15) Metochos, ver. 7; koinonos, ver. 10. see Notes, Heb. 2.14.
praying. (e-13) Lit. 'And (or 'But') he was withdrawing himself in the deserts and praying.' He was at that time waiting, occupied with prayer.
new (b-16) 'New' is kainos, when used here of 'garment,' neos of 'wine.' see Note, Heb. 12.24. rend (c-26) Or 'cut up.'
new (b-5) 'New' is kainos, when used here of 'garment,' neos of 'wine.' see Note, Heb. 12.24.
new, (b-11) 'New' is kainos, when used here of 'garment,' neos of 'wine.' see Note, Heb. 12.24.

second-first (d-8) The expression 'second-first sabbath' is explained thus. The year, as regards the worship of God amongst the Jews, began with the month Abib (Heb. 'green corn'), which lasted from the middle of March to the middle of April. In Leviticus 23, in which we find the Jewish feasts described, we may observe that in addition to the general and weekly recurring feasts of the sabbath, the chief feasts begin with the passover (the 14th of Abib), and that, in immediate connexion with it, it was ordained that on the day after the following sabbath the first-fruits of the corn should be offered in the ear, a foreshadowing of the resurrection of Jesus which took place on the morrow after the sabbath of the passover week, or feast of unleavened bread. The sabbath immediately following the passover was therefore the 'first' or great sabbath, and after the offering of the first-fruits on the morrow after the sabbath, the first day of the week, the harvest might be commenced, and the new corn eaten, which was not permitted before, even though corn stood ripe in the fields. On the following sabbath, the 'second' after the 'first' or great sabbath, we see that the disciples ate ears of corn on the way, for the offering of the first-fruits had already taken place on the first day of the week; and, as seven weeks or sabbaths were counted from this day to the feast of Pentecost, it was therefore the 'first' of these seven sabbaths, or the 'second' with reference to the great sabbath of the Passover.
not (a-7) not (a-15) A strong negative. 'in no wise.'

given (b-21) Lit. 'they shall give.' in ver. 44, 'they gather not' and 'they vintage not.' An example of Luke's use of the third person active of a verb impersonally with a passive sense. Also chs. 12.20; 14.35; 16.4,9; 23.31.

gathered (b-14) Lit. 'they shall give.' in ver. 44, 'they gather not' and 'they vintage not.' An example of Luke's use of the third person active of a verb impersonally with a passive sense. Also chs. 12.20; 14.35; 16.4,9; 23.31.
save (a-21) Or 'cure,' 'make perfectly well.' see Matt. 14.36.
afterwards (b-6) Or 'on the following [day].' see ch. 9.37.
kissed (d-27) Or 'ardently kissed,' 'covered with kisses;' so ver. 45. cf. ch. 15.20; Acts 20.37.
were, (c-8) Or 'into the thorns.' life, (d-27) Bios, life as such in this world.
who (e-10) Or 'who are such as;' so ver. 3.
besought (d-3) Or 'he besought.' pit. (e-17) The word elsewhere translated 'abyss;' Rom. 10.7; Rev. 9.1, &c.
gladly, (a-13) 'Received with welcome.' see Acts 15.4. It is only used by Luke, ch. 9.11; Acts 2.41; 15.4; 18.27; 24.3; 28.30.
one (a-12) Lit. 'a prophet, one of the old [ones].'
hand-baskets. (b-25) Possibly 'twelve hand-baskets of fragments.' see Matt. 16.9
one (c-14) Or 'some prophet of the old ones.' see Note a.

lose (e-10) lose (e-15) I am not satisfied with 'lose' here, but it must be read in connexion with what immediately follows. The word is the same as 'destroyed' in ver. 25. It means both 'lose' and 'destroy.' see Rom. 14.15; 1Cor. 8.11, 'perish.'
not (f-18) A strong negative. 'in no wise.'
who (c-8) Hostis. as Matt. 7.24; 'who indeed,' or 'who were no other than.'

overshadowed (e-13) See Note, Matt. 17.5. they (f-19) Some authorities read 'those,' but I have put 'they' (i.e. the disciples (Ed.)), with other authorities, as it seems a change made to refer it to Moses and Elias.
Master, (d-5) As ch. 5.5. forbad (a-18) Or 'hindered,' 'prohibited,' as ch. 11.52; Matt. 19.14.
are]. (c-15) The words in brackets are, to say the least, doubtful.
have; (d-14) Or 'as may be [offered you] by them.'
power (b-6) Exousia. see Matt. 10.1. The second 'power' in this verse is 'dunamis'.

justifying (e-5) Aorist tense; difficult to express in English. It gives the sense that he wanted to make out that he was in that state, not that he was obtaining it. see ch. 9.60,61, where 'suffer,' 'allow,' and 'bid adieu' are all aorists.
Although (c-6) Or 'even though.' rate, (d-28) As Luke 18.5; 1Cor. 9.2.
give (e-25) Or 'who from heaven will give.'
armed (b-5) Lit. 'fully armed;' only here. 'panoply' only here and Eph. 6.11,13. house, (c-9) Or 'court.' see Note. Matt. 26.69.
panoply (b-16) Lit. 'fully armed;' only here. 'panoply' only here and Eph. 6.11,13.
first, (b-26) Some read 'first of all beware.' but needlessly, I think. It was the first thing on his heart to tell them. Beware (c-27) See Note to Matt. 16.6.
denied (f-12) A stronger word (as Matt. 16.24; 26.34) than the first 'denied' here.
soul, (a-7) Soul, (a-8) 'Life' and 'soul' are the same in Greek, but not in ver. 15.
required (b-13) Lit. 'they shall require.' see Note, ch. 6.38.
life, (a-18) 'Life' and 'soul' are the same in Greek, but not in ver. 15.
life (a-2) 'Life' and 'soul' are the same in Greek, but not in ver. 15.

not, (e-2) There is an emphatic article here, impossible to translate into English. '[you who are] the little flock.' It is the character Christ gives to them as attached to him in the midst of the world.
[bondmen]. (a-22) 'Bondmen' is doubtful. This would make 'those' more emphatic.

For (b-1) The 'For' here is the practical conclusion the Lord draws as to the need of Israel's reconciling itself with God. 'Hearing what I say, that is what you have to do.' lest (c-21) See Notes, Matt. 5.25 and Mark 4.12.
mite. (a-20) * The smallest current coin of that day.
saved (c-13) Spared in the judgment of the nation by Messiah, so as to enter into the kingdom. 'the remnant.' See Isa. 10.21-22; Acts 2.47.
I (a-20) not. (a-37) Lit. 'I desired' -- 'ye desired not.' see Matt. 23.37.
not (b-16) A strengthened negative. Lord. (c-35) 'Jehovah.' see Ps. 118.26.
out. (b-13) Lit 'they cast it out.' see ch. 6.38.
coming (a-9) Lit. 'drawing near;' not only at this time; it is usual.
of. (d-32) 'what they had to live on,' as 'substance,' 1John 3.17.
husks (e-10) The word translated 'husks' is a food called St. John's bread; it was eaten by animals and sometimes by destitute persons.
kisses. (f-40) 'Covered him with kisses.' As ch. 7.38; Matt. 26.49; Mark 14.45; Acts 20.37.
serve (a-13) Douleuo. bond-service, i.e. of a slave.
mocked (e-13) The word translated 'mocked' only occurs here and at ch. 23.35, where it is rendered 'sneered.'
received (c-10) The word means, 'to receive all,' 'the sum of what we have to get.'
offences (d-12) Skandalon. It means the part of a fall-trap that makes the trap fall when touched. see Note, Matt. 13.57.
snare (d-28) Skandalon. It means the part of a fall-trap that makes the trap fall when touched. see Note, Matt. 13.57. millstone (e-10) Or 'a great millstone,' as in Matt. 18.6.
immediately (a-28) Or 'will immediately say [to him], Come and ...'
city, (b-8) Lit. 'a certain judge in a certain city.'
gain. (e-11) See Notes at Luke 21.19 and 1Thess. 4.4.
things (a-9) Some read, 'left what was our own.'

bondmen, (a-7) Or 'ten bondmen of his.' minas, (b-13) Mina. see Note, Ezek. 45.12. coming. (c-22) The same sense as 'till I come;' he was to go and return (ver. 12); while he was away and not yet come they were to trade.
them, (d-13) In ver. 14 the expression is the same, but with a change of tense.
wept (b-10) Not only weeping, as Mark 9.24, but audible expression of grief, as ch. 22.62; Rom. 12.15; Phil. 3.18; Rev. 5.4, &c.
written, (a-13) Ps. 118.22. corner-stone? (b-25) Lit. 'head of corner.'
they (d-16) i.e. the 'suborned persons.' see ver. 26.
bush, (a-14) See Note at Mark 2.26. Lord (b-19) 'Jehovah.' see Mark 12.26. Jacob; (c-33) Ex. 3.6.
judgment. (f-19) Krima, the sentence passed on the thing charged as guilt, even the charge itself as ground of judgment; not the fact of condemnation.

souls. (b-7) Or 'possess your souls.' In the first sense, that of the text, it is the same thought as Matt. 24.13; Luke 17.33; Matt. 16.25; Luke 9.24, &c.. see Mark 13.13. For the second, the Greek certainly means 'possess,' as 'owners,' Acts 4.34. See 1Thess. 4.4, which evidently does not mean 'obtain a wife,' as alleged. There is the idea in the word of 'having by getting.' see Matt. 10.9; Luke 18.12. The idea is, 'they would have Messiah's deliverance,' and it is so worded as to allow that it would be a better deliverance to the killed, though some would win life here below.
temple, (d-9) abroad (e-17) As 'passed the night,' Matt. 21.17.
restored, (d-19) Lit. 'hast returned back;' 'confirm' is sterizo, as 'establish,' Rom. 16.25; 1Pet. 5.10.
remitted (a-10) Remitted is the technical word for sending to one's proper jurisdiction. So, ver. 11, 'sent back' alludes probably to jurisdiction, as they were in strife about it.
back (a-23) Remitted is the technical word for sending to one's proper jurisdiction. So, ver. 11, 'sent back' alludes probably to jurisdiction, as they were in strife about it.
sabbath, (d-7) Or 'on the first [day] of the week.'
by (e-19) Same expression as 'was there by,' ch. 2.9. shining (f-22) As 'lightens,' ch. 17.24.
Nazaraean, (b-18) Some read 'Nazarene,' as Mark 1.24. prophet (c-22) Lit. 'a man, a prophet.'
gave (f-23) It has the sense of 'giving it into their hands,' as a letter. as ver. 42; ch. 4.17. He took the house-father's place, and blessed and gave it to them.
gave (a-3) Same as 'gave' in ver. 30. see Note.
it (b-4) Or 'took it before them and ate.'
